Hosts: none here, all three there. Pays the three-host install-and-run round once for two back-to-back renames that ship in one release with nothing released between them, so no run is spent verifying a state no user will ever install. Breaks the stated rule outright: `main` stands with `host_tests/`, the agent files, and every host definition changed and unverified on any host until the next work runs, a failure found then cannot be told apart between the two renames, and if the plugin rename slips or is reshaped the debt has no owner.

Timing: before each commit of this work that touches a trigger set, as `CONTRIBUTING.md` ## Development states the rule. Hosts: every host whose set that commit touches, which is all three for any commit touching `core/agents/*.md`, `scripts/build_hosts.py`, or `host_tests/`, and the one host for a commit touching only that host's definition directory. Each run passes before its commit lands; nothing is left to the plugin rename's work. Follows the stated rule exactly, so the work sets no precedent of skipping it, and a failure is pinned to the one commit that caused it rather than traced back across the whole rename. The costliest position: a hard-cut rename lands as many commits, each touching shared paths, and every Antigravity and Codex run first needs the built tree copied or installed by hand into that host's installed location, since the suite stops when the copy differs from the committed tree; it also forces the tasks to be ordered so that every intermediate commit leaves the tools, the skills, and `host_tests/` (which itself invokes `--milestone`, writes `Milestone directory:` lines, and builds `Milestone-definition:` and `Milestone-finish:` commits) consistent enough to pass, which a half-renamed tree may not be; and the plugin rename pays the same three-host runs again directly after.

Timing: before each commit of this work that touches a trigger set. Hosts: Claude Code only, whose installed copy is the working tree's `hosts/claude/` under the directory marketplace and so is current after each rebuild with no install step. Antigravity and Codex: not run in this work; their runs are left to the plugin rename's work. Keeps the per-commit failure localisation for every host-neutral path (the agent files, the build, `host_tests/` and its fixture, the renamed discovery and flag) at the price of one CLI run per commit and no hand install. Departs from the rule for two hosts: the slot value files and README templates in the Antigravity and Codex definitions, including the dispatch slots that carry `<MILESTONE_DIR>`, stand on `main` unverified on those hosts until the plugin rename runs them, and a failure found then cannot be told apart from one that rename caused; per-commit runs still force every intermediate commit to be passable, and the run copy being the working tree depends on which copy runs this milestone's tasks, an axis the running-copy question owns.

Timing: once, after the last renaming change and before the milestone is finished, against the tree `main` ends in, rather than before each commit. Hosts: all three, each brought up to date by its documented install and run until it passes. Nothing is left to the plugin rename's work. Verifies on every host exactly the state this work promises to leave, `main` consistent under the new word, while sparing the intermediate half-renamed commits a bar they cannot meet and paying each host's install and run once. Bends the per-commit letter of the rule for the commits in between, so a failure found at the end has to be traced across the whole rename; the three-host cost is still paid twice in a row, once here and once by the plugin rename touching the same sets; and whether the Claude Code copy compared is the working tree at the run depends on which copy runs this milestone, an axis the running-copy question owns.

Timing: once, after the last renaming change and before the milestone is finished. Hosts: Claude Code only.
